sections.h2: Why can a Frankfort house have two tax bills?
sections.html:
Because the City of Frankfort taxes inside its limits on top of the county. Everyone in Franklin County gets a county bill from the Franklin County Sheriff, and a house in Frankfort also gets a city bill from the Finance Office, which collects for Frankfort Independent Schools too.

The Franklin County PVA sets the values for both bills. The county lists the office at 313 West Main Street, 2nd Floor, Room 209, Frankfort, with a fax at (502) 226-5495 and a phone at (502) 875-8780, open weekdays from 8:00 until 4:30. The sheriff moved to the Public Safety Complex at 974 River Bend Road and answers at (502) 875-8740. The sheriff's website offers a tax bill search with card payment, and the front door has a secure drop box under camera watch.

Frankfort says it works from the PVA's figure, which is 100 percent of fair market value as of each January 1. Questions about a value, an exemption or a mailing address belong with the PVA, not the city.

sections.h2: How do the county and Frankfort calendars differ?
sections.html:
The city does not copy the state schedule. County bills follow KRS 134.015, while Frankfort publishes its own dates, so a deadline that works for one bill can already be past for the other.

Sheriff bill and City of Frankfort bill side by side (sources: KRS 134.015, City of Frankfort Finance Office)
FeatureCounty billCity of Frankfort bill
Early-payment credit2 percent off when paid in full by November 12 percent off for money received before November 30

After the deadline5 percent in January, then 10 percent10 percent plus interest

The city also reminds owners with escrow accounts to hand the bill to the servicer, since the lender cannot pay what it never received. City commissioners vote the city rate each year on the finance director's advice, and Frankfort Independent Schools sets the old city school rate.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Franklin County for a seller?
sections.html:
Franklin County is the seat of state government, and it is more urban than most of Kentucky. It was carved out in 1795 from Woodford, Mercer and Shelby counties, and the lines of Kentucky's three original counties once met inside what is now Franklin County. The land area is 208 square miles, and six counties touch it: Owen, Scott, Woodford, Anderson, Shelby and Henry.

Interstate 64 serves the county, along with US 60, US 127, US 421, US 460 and KY 676, and Frankfort Transit runs buses. Two school systems share the area. Franklin County Public Schools covers nearly all of it, including most of Frankfort, while Frankfort Independent Schools covers downtown, South Frankfort around the Capitol, and Bellepoint. Kentucky State University is here too. Recreation includes Josephine Sculpture Park, Cove Spring Park and the wooded trails on Fort Hill, where Union troops dug earthworks before an 1864 skirmish.

Growth has been steady rather than fast. The population was 5,078 in 1800, reached 49,285 in 2010 and stood at 51,541 in 2020. The 2025 estimate of 52,649 is 2.1 percent above the 2020 base.

sections.h2: What do Franklin County's economy and housing numbers show?
sections.html:
• Typical house value, 2020 to 2024 survey: $216,600, roughly double the Floyd County figure.
  • Owners live in 64.5 percent of homes, which leaves a large rental share.
  • Housing units: 24,404 in 2025. Households: 22,718, averaging 2.20 people.
  • Median gross rent: $967. Median household income: $65,298, with 12.3 percent below the poverty line.
  • Permits for new homes in 2025: 96.
  • Commute: 20.0 minutes on average, and 62.2 percent of adults are in the labor force.
  • Education: 92.8 percent finished high school and 31.9 percent hold a bachelor's degree or more.

State employment shows up in the data. Employer businesses numbered 1,278 in 2023 with 16,897 jobs and a payroll near $869 million, and retail sales topped $1 billion in 2022. About 73 percent of the population lived in an urban area in 2020, so sellers in Frankfort face a deeper buyer pool than most Kentucky counties can offer, and a bill that is larger in dollars.

Health care brought in about $397 million in 2022, and the county counts 3,768 businesses with no employees besides the owner. Vacancy was low when the 2020 census was taken: 9.0 percent of the county's 24,000 housing units stood empty, compared with 13.8 percent in Floyd County. A seller carrying a tax balance should collect payoff figures from both billing offices before picking a closing date.

sections.h2: How does an owner appeal a Franklin County assessment?
sections.html:
Meet the PVA first, because the state will not take an appeal from an owner who skipped the conference. The roll is posted for 13 days beginning in the first week of May, and the PVA has to advertise that period in the county's largest newspaper.

Next, file at the county clerk's office by the end of the following business day. A local board of assessment appeals then hears cases roughly four or five weeks later. It listens only to evidence offered with you and the PVA both present, so bring comparable sales, a recent appraisal, repair estimates or insurance records. You may audio-record the hearing, and the board owes you a written explanation of any change. If bills have already printed when the board raises a value, a supplemental bill makes up the gap.

sections.h2: Does Franklin County offer a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
It does for seniors and totally disabled owners. The state exemption is $49,100 in 2025 and 2026, deducted from assessed value before tax is calculated. A house worth the county median of $216,600 would be taxed on $167,500.

File with the Franklin County PVA. Ask that office how the January 1 ownership date applies if you buy or sell partway through a year, and tell it about any sale so the exemption comes off the old address.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Franklin County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
It follows the parcel to the closing table. KRS 134.015 treats the tax as the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and a delinquency lien survives a change of ownership.

Open bills pass from the sheriff to the county clerk on April 15. From then on 1 percent interest accrues every month, the clerk takes a 10 percent commission, and a county attorney commission of 20 percent applies after the first notice goes out.

  • Ask the sheriff for a payoff at (502) 875-8740, and the city Finance Office at (502) 875-8500 if the house is in Frankfort.
  • Have the title company pay both bills from your proceeds so the policy issues clean.
  • A buyer that purchases as-is and closes quickly can take over a house with arrears and repairs without a listing period.

faqs.q: Do Frankfort homeowners pay the city and the county?
faqs.a: Yes. They receive a county bill collected by the sheriff and a city bill collected by the Finance Office, which also collects for Frankfort Independent Schools.

faqs.q: Where is the Franklin County sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: It is at 974 River Bend Road, Frankfort, KY 40601, and the phone is (502) 875-8740. Bills can also be searched and paid on the sheriff's website.

faqs.q: Where is the Franklin County PVA?
faqs.a: It is at 313 West Main Street, 2nd Floor, Room 209, Frankfort, KY 40601. The phone is (502) 875-8780, and the county lists weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:30.

faqs.q: How big is the Franklin County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Seniors and totally disabled owners apply through the PVA, and the amount is subtracted from the assessed value.

faqs.q: How soon after April 15 can Franklin County hold a tax sale?
faqs.a: The sale must fall between 90 and 135 days after the sheriff transfers the bills to the clerk, and the county attorney mails notices beforehand.
